items.text: Table API refactor in the v4 cycle (Jan-Feb 2020): the table stores the next document ID instead of the last, process_docs was removed, internal read/update methods were renamed, `Table.contains` accepts only a single doc ID (list semantics were ambiguous), and `len(table)` performance was improved. Related fixes covered document ID generation, doc ID conversion in updates and `len(db)` on empty databases. Goal: simplify the API and make behavior unambiguous.

v3.12.1 of tinydb was released on 2018-11-09 (version bump by Markus Siemens), containing the fix 'Don't break when searching the same query multiple times' by Andrew Reilly: a bugfix for repeated identical query searches breaking.

Table.update and Table.remove now skip missing doc_ids instead of raising KeyError (#616, fixes #591, 2026-05-21). IDs are filtered inside the updater before side effects so operations are atomic and consistent with Table.get; upsert dropped its unreachable except KeyError branch. Previously mixed existing/missing IDs caused partial in-memory mutation before KeyError, since documents are shared by reference.

Related fixes covered document ID generation, doc ID conversion in updates and `len(db)` on empty databases. | When: January-February 2020 | Involving: Markus Siemens | Simplify the API and make method behavior unambiguous

items.text: v4.0 architecture refactor (November 2019, rationale in #284): Python 2 support removed, `ujson` support and the deprecated element ID API deprecated/removed, new architecture adopted, type annotations and subclassing helpers (Extension Mechanisms) added, and project configuration moved to Poetry. Goal: modernize the codebase with a cleaner architecture and extension mechanisms.
YAML support work in tinydb: commits added PyYAML to setup.py and ensured YAML tests are run, so the dependency is declared and YAML functionality is part of the test run.

Query hashing/matching fixes (2026-08 to 2026-10): Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes/bytearray as sequences (is_sequence uses collections.abc.Sequence) (#641, fixes #638); Query.test freezes unhashable list/dict args to avoid TypeError when hashed (#618, fixes #517); regex flags are included in the matches/search query hash so case-insensitive and case-sensitive searches don't share a cache entry (#640, fixes #637). These were correctness bugs: wrong matches and cache poisoning/TypeErrors on hashing.
